newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan oil slick washes ashore.
newsitem.headline: Japan oil slick washes ashore.

text.p: Japan's worst oil spill from a supertanker in Tokyo Bay spread overnight and small quantities of oil washed ashore early on Thursday in the heavily populated areas of Yokohama and Kawasaki, a coastguard spokesman said.

Parts of the slick from an estimated 15,000 tonnes of oil spilled onto one of Japan's busiest waterways reached the breakwater on the shores of three areas, and clean-up operations were under way, he said.
"Some oil has reached ashore and more is approaching," a coastguard spokesman told Reuters.
He said apart from the three points where oil had already washed ashore, parts of the slick were nearing two other areas on the shoreline of Chiba prefecture.
On Wednesday, the Panamanian-registered supertanker Diamond Grace struck a reef off Yokohama, rupturing at least two of its crude oil tanks.

The ship, a very large crude carrier (VLCC) carrying a total of 257,000 tonnes of crude oil from the United Arab Emirates to a refinery in Kawasaki, south of Tokyo, has leaked an estimated 15,000 tonnes of crude oil, making it the worst oil spill accident in Japan.
